issues.reason: The exact CollisionAvoidance composite and all of its children are outside the finite root-reachable set. Consequently, the required operating scope cannot be entered through the model's top-level initial behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The collision avoidance composite has a local initial edge, but no supplied fact connects its enclosing composite to the top-level initial reachability graph; local entry therefore does not establish root reachability.
issues.title: Collision avoidance scope is unreachable from root

issues.basis: NL12 source transition tr_0027; closed transition transition:line:87; event-consumer fact lists transition:line:87 as the only consumer and an empty reachable consumer set; finite verify event-consumer check is refuted.
issues.expected: The activation event has a reachable consumer transition within the collision avoidance system scope.
issues.observed: The sole consumer transition is transition:line:87 from state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:84 to state:collision_avoidance_active:line:85, and reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty.
issues.reason: The activation transition exists and is declared as the consumer, but the exact consumer state and transition are unreachable from a top-level initial entry. Declaration does not provide operational coverage.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The consumer transition is structurally present and its event is declared, but the supplied reachability facts provide no reachable execution path to that consumer.
issues.title: Collision activation consumer is unreachable

issues.basis: NL10 termination contract and source transition tr_0025; closed model shows the termination target state:FinishState:line:21, FinishState outgoing transitions transition:line:36 and transition:line:40, and enclosing AutonomousMode self-loop transition:line:90; source/model ancestry differs from a stable final completion boundary.
issues.expected: UrbanMode eventually and stably terminates at FinishState without continued behavior through the target or active ancestors.
issues.observed: UrbanMode's completion route enters state:FinishState:line:21, which has outgoing transitions, while AutonomousMode has a reachable self-transition transition:line:90; the supplied model therefore retains continuation behavior after reaching the named target.
issues.reason: The exact FinishState endpoint exists, but the designated termination state is nested in HighwayMode and the closed model retains continuation paths through the enclosing hierarchy, including a self-loop on AutonomousMode and routes involving FinishState. Endpoint existence alone does not establish stable termination.
issues.requirement_quote: The system exits the UrbanMode state by transitioning to FinishState once `auto_finished=true` is satisfied.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: FinishState is the named completion target and the endpoint transition exists, but the supplied closed-model inventory also explicitly records outgoing target and ancestor continuations, so endpoint existence cannot rebut the broader termination property.
issues.title: Urban termination target has continued behavior
